eval-smoke-baseline.success_criteria: the /eval smoke run reports PASS (no metric drop >2% vs the saved baseline)

argv:
code-review-gate has NO portable default.

This gate id resolved, but the skill-bundled default cannot review anything: there is
no model-invocable working-diff reviewer to bind a gate to. /code-review is WORSE than unlaunchable: it ships
disable-model-invocation: FALSE, so a skill-kind mapping to it DOES run -- and it fans
finder agents over the REPO ROOT, discarding whatever scope the gate set (2026-08-23: 12
agents, 426 tool calls, 110M cache-read tokens, no verdict at the 1800s wall). Bind a
review gate to llm-review-low|medium|high instead. /review does carry
disable-model-invocation: true, and because verify-gates.md has the orchestrator judge a
skill gate 'from its output', an unlaunchable skill gate is indistinguishable from a passing one.
That silent pass shipped twice (2026-07-26 and its remap). This deliberate failure is
the fix: a gate you cannot run must be loud, not green.

Define it in <project>/.claude/eval-gates.json. Project entries win over these
defaults, so a local definition makes this message go away. Prefer kind: argv -- an
exit code cannot be self-attested. Worked example (example-project):

  "code-review-gate": {
    "kind": "argv",
    "argv": ["bash", "scripts/session-quality-gate.sh"],
    "cwd": ".", "timeout": 900
  }

That script lints, type-checks and import-checks the Python the session actually
changed -- detected from the WORKING TREE, because verify gates run before
post_session commits, so any committed-delta detection sees nothing and passes.
If the session genuinely needs an LLM review, make it a require_evidence artifact
instead of a gate.
code-review-gate.success_criteria: FAILS BY DESIGN until the project defines code-review-gate in its own .claude/eval-gates.json. There is no portable reviewer to default to, and a gate that cannot run must be loud rather than green. The id is kept in the bundled vocabulary so existing plans still BUILD (build_plan.py rejects unknown gate ids); only execution fails, with instructions.
code-review-gate._note: REWRITTEN 2026-07-28. Was kind: skill -> `code-review`, which is disable-model-invocation and cannot be launched by any agent: silently unrunnable for every session that declared it and had no project-local override. A 2026-07-26 project-side remap to skill `review` reproduced the bug (same flag, and `review` is a routing alias, not a reviewer). Reproduced live: the same probe plan returned invoke-skill/code-review from outside a .claude root and run-argv from inside a project that defines the gate locally -- i.e. every plan built outside a .claude root inherited the silent no-op.

test-orchestrate.success_criteria: all tests pass (exit-zero outcome from test-orchestrate); any remaining failure is a gate failure that triggers rework

llm-review-low.success_criteria: exit 0. Runs `claude -p "/code-review low" --output-format json` against the session's diff -- `git diff $PLAN_EXECUTE_REVIEW_BASE` when that names the commit the session started from, else `git diff HEAD` -- and parses the reviewer's findings block. PASS REQUIRES A PARSEABLE, EMPTY FINDINGS BLOCK -- exit 0 from the CLI is NOT enough. Three outcomes: 0 = empty findings block; 1 = >=1 finding; 2 = INDETERMINATE (no parseable block after one retry, or empty/invalid stdout, or is_error). 2 is a FAILURE, never a pass: a headless session can exit 0 having emitted nothing, and a gate that cannot tell 'no findings' from 'no output' is the silent-green bug this framework already shipped twice. Intent-into-review: PLAN_EXECUTE_INTENT_FILE (or --intent-file) feeds the session's ## Work text to the reviewer inside UNTRUSTED-DATA markers so a deliberate choice classifies ask-user; the exit code is computed from the findings count alone, so intent can only downgrade an action, never clear a finding. AN EMPTY REVIEWED SURFACE IS INDETERMINATE, NOT A PASS: once a session COMMITS its work `git diff HEAD` is empty, the reviewer is handed nothing, and its empty findings array reads as green -- measured on every session of the model-portability plan. Set PLAN_EXECUTE_REVIEW_BASE (or --base) to the session's starting commit so committed work is reviewed; an unresolvable base is INDETERMINATE too, since it diffs nothing. THE REVIEWED SURFACE IS THIS SESSION'S, NOT THE WORKING TREE'S: with PLAN_EXECUTE_PLAN_DIR (and PLAN_EXECUTE_SESSION) set, untracked files under ANOTHER plan, or under another session's _evidence/, are dropped -- measured on s03, where 5 of 6 blocking findings were against already-EXECUTED evidence scripts the session could not fix, since editing a script after it produced a recorded result destroys the thing that makes it evidence. Every dropped path is PRINTED with its reason: an exclusion that silently shrinks the surface is the same silent-green class as the empty surface above. Unset plan context means the rule cannot be evaluated and does not fire.
llm-review-low._note: ADDED (plan-framework-upgrade s10, RV-01) on the strength of s01's BINDABLE probe verdict, which proved main-tree AND in-worktree binding -- both matter, because isolated parallel-group members run their gates inside their own worktree. PROVEN BEFORE INSTALL, not asserted: fixtures/llm-review-gate/rerun.sh plants an off-by-one, runs every INSTALLED level, and exits non-zero if the plant is missed, if the clean allow-control fails, if an intent block claiming the bug is deliberate clears it, or if any of the three captured INDETERMINATE responses (empty result / conversational summary with no findings block / zero-byte stdout, all exit 0) passes. The harness runs under the same restricted env allowlist run_deploy_argv imposes in production. Distinct from code-review-gate ON PURPOSE: that id is the DETERMINISTIC pytest/lint gate and is not overloaded. TIMEOUTS are 4x the slowest wall measured on a ~10-line fixture diff (31s at this level); a real multi-file diff reviews slower, so if this ever times out raise it from a MEASURED run rather than guessing -- a timeout arrives in the feedback file as one line and is indistinguishable from a real finding. TIMEOUTS REALIGNED TO THE MEASURED VALUES 2026-08-21: this bundled default had drifted BELOW the gearbox project copy at all three levels (low 180/420, medium 900/2000, high 660/1380) while the project copy carried values raised from real measured runs. The project copy WINS, so gearbox never felt it -- but a fresh checkout, an adopting repo, and the deployed ~/.claude tree all run THIS file, and each would stall INDETERMINATE on a clock exactly as the raising session did. A note in this registry says 'if you change one, change the other'; three separate raises had changed only one. Now low 300/720, medium 1500/3200, high 1500/3120. Medium's figure is the measurement: a 46-file / 5,147-line surface exceeded 900s TWICE, and scaling the measured 660s@25-files to 46 gives ~1,215s, so 1500s is that plus ~23% slack. Raise again only from another measured run, and prefer SHRINKING the reviewed surface -- at 46 files one pass is sampling, not covering.
llm-review-low.timeout_note: RAISED (inner 300 -> 1200, registry 720 -> 2400) after a REAL INDETERMINATE, not a guess. plan example-review-plan-2026-08-25 s02: the reviewer exceeded --timeout 300s on BOTH attempts over a 3-file / 176-line surface, and the gate returned INDETERMINATE with nothing reviewed. The 300s budget came from 4x a 31s ~10-line fixture run, which the _note itself flagged as optimistic for a real multi-file diff. Measured context on the same box the same day: this gate answered in ~180s per session under light load, and timed out twice at 300s under heavy machine load. The binding constraint is BOX CONTENTION, not surface size. 1200s is 4x the budget that demonstrably failed and stays below llm-review-medium's 1800s inner. Re-measure and tighten if a loaded run ever comes in well under this. CONFIRMED: the very next run of this same gate/surface passed in 294s under the same contention — i.e. the old 300s budget was MARGINAL, not wildly wrong, which is why it read as a flaky INDETERMINATE rather than an obvious misconfiguration. 1200s keeps the note's own 4x-the-slowest-measured convention against that 294s.

cross-family-review-low.success_criteria: exit 0. Same contract as `llm-review-low`, but `--reviewer codex` routes the review to a Codex CLI process instead of the on-box Claude reviewer -- CROSS-FAMILY: the family that did NOT write the code reviews it, on the premise that a model most often MISSES the bug categories it most often PRODUCES. Runs `codex exec` (headless, JSON) against the session's diff -- `git diff $PLAN_EXECUTE_REVIEW_BASE` when that names the commit the session started from, else `git diff HEAD` -- and parses the reviewer's findings block. PASS REQUIRES A PARSEABLE, EMPTY FINDINGS BLOCK -- exit 0 from the CLI is NOT enough. Three outcomes: 0 = empty findings block; 1 = >=1 finding; 2 = INDETERMINATE (no parseable block after one retry, or empty/invalid stdout, or is_error). 2 is a FAILURE, never a pass. THIS GATE IS READ-ONLY: it raises findings, it never rewrites code. RESTRICTED-REPO BEHAVIOUR: a tree that trips the egress/data-sensitivity guard, or a codex that is reachable but unusable (not installed, not logged in, quota-exhausted), never completes a real review -- the backend prints `VERIFIER: on_box_human` / `DEGRADED_FROM: cross_family` (or `cross_family_unavailable`) within the first 10 lines of stdout and exits 2 (INDETERMINATE). verify.py reads those markers BY PREFIX over the whole stdout, with no fixed line window (line 1 stays the reviewer identity line), and parks the session at AWAITS_REVIEW: no rework is charged, no escalation rung is armed, and a human records the disposition with `run.py ack-checkpoint --session <sid> --decision verified-on-box|blocked` (verified-on-box finishes the verify pass and lets shipping proceed; blocked stops the session and ships nothing). A plain ack with no --decision is REFUSED. HARNESS-AWARE (PLAN_EXECUTE_HARNESS, derived from the session's own dispatch_started/dispatch_families record in run.ndjson): under the codex harness the family that did NOT write the code is CLAUDE, so the gate degrades the SAME way unless model-routing.yaml sets verification.claude_verifier_under_codex_harness: true. An exit 2 with NO marker is a TRANSPORT failure instead -- the reviewer could not run -- and re-runs free of charge up to a bounded budget before becoming a blocker that names the transport cause. A plan whose sessions BUILD this gate cannot use it on itself -- it would be reviewing the reviewer's own untrusted output. Intent-into-review, the reviewed-surface rules (base/scope/exclude), and the three-outcome contract are IDENTICAL to llm-review-* -- see verify-gates.md's 'Cross-family review' subsection.
cross-family-review-low.timeout_note: RAISED (inner 300 -> 1200, registry 720 -> 2400), in lockstep with `llm-review-low`, which was raised from the same pair in the same commit after a REAL INDETERMINATE: plan example-review-plan-2026-08-25 s02 exceeded --timeout 300s on BOTH attempts over a 3-file / 176-line surface under box contention (heavy machine load). This entry shipped 300/720 for one commit because it was copied from `llm-review-low` BEFORE that raise landed. The binding constraint is box contention, not reviewer family, and the review shape is identical (one headless CLI call against a scoped diff file), so the twin's measured budget applies here unchanged. See `llm-review-low`'s own timeout_note for the measurement. Re-measure and tighten if a loaded codex run ever comes in well under this.
cross-family-review-low._note: ADDED (cross-family-review-gate WIRE-01). Reuses llm-review-*'s own registry timeouts LEVEL FOR LEVEL -- each cross-family level carries the same inner/outer pair as its llm-review-* twin (low 1200/2400, medium 1800/4000, high 1500/3120) -- rather than sizing from the live smoke measurement: s01b's CODEX_LIVE=1 run (real `codex exec`, planted eval() defect, _evidence/s01b/live-smoke.txt) measured 30-131s per level on a 1-file/8-line diff -- comfortably inside every one of these budgets -- but that diff is a fixture, not a real session surface. Real sessions in this plan's own ledger run 16->32 and 41->47 files; llm-review-*'s numbers were raised from MEASURED multi-file surfaces (46 files exceeding 900s twice, see llm-review-medium's _note) and the review shape (one headless CLI call against a scoped diff file) is identical between the two reviewer families, so borrowing those numbers sizes for the largest surface this plan can justify rather than the smallest it measured. Distinct from code-review-gate and llm-review-* ON PURPOSE: code-review-gate is the deterministic pytest/lint gate; llm-review-* is the on-box (Claude) reviewer; cross-family-review-* is the SAME review contract routed to codex via --reviewer. If a real run ever times out, raise from a MEASURED multi-file run per level, exactly as llm-review-*'s history did, and keep the pair equal to its llm-review-* twin unless a measurement says otherwise. REGISTRY HOME, measured: these three ids live in THIS bundled default ONLY -- the gearbox project copy `.claude/eval-gates.json` carries `code-review-gate` and the three `llm-review-*` ids and none of the cross-family ones. That is deliberate, not an omission: `shipping._load_registry` merges bundled-then-project, so a bundled-only id resolves everywhere while a project entry still wins where one exists. If a project copy ever DOES add these ids, land the same number in both (see verify-gates.md's two-registries note).

Intent-into-review, the reviewed-surface rules (base/scope/exclude), and the three-outcome contract are IDENTICAL to llm-review-* -- see verify-gates.md's 'Cross-family review' subsection.
